edit.description: `placementKey` (:763) spells the `(host, kind, key)` triple with a private U+001F separator, and `member-address.ts`'s `nestedAddress` (:60) already spells that exact triple as `<host>/<kind>/<key>` — the declared one home for every member-identity spelling, which this module already imports (:21) and already uses for the same triple at `declaredAddresses` (:1048). `placementKey`'s own doc admits it: 'the same triple the `nested_member` row it feeds is identified by'. Retire `placementKey`, key `nestedMemberRow`'s placement/extent lookup (:823) by `nestedAddress`, and re-point the `EdgePlacements`/`RenderedExtents` doc links (:768, :785). The U+001F separator is not the thing to preserve: it guards a private in-memory Map against a `/`-in-key ambiguity the public grammar already admits for the member table itself, so the protection sits at the wrong layer — moving the stronger separator *into* `member-address.ts` would change the address grammar on both sides of the seam (`src/member_address.rs`, whose module header names this residue class with this entry's own `per` cite) and is explicitly not this entry.

The three loops that iterate the identical set — every composed embedded value of every `blocks()` member — and key it by the identical `(hostAddress(kind, name), value.kind, value.key)` triple, two through `placementKey` and one through `nestedAddress`: `edgePlacements` (:512), `renderedExtents` (:552), `nestedTargets` (:795). Their own docs already assert the sets coincide ('Iterates exactly the values `nestedMemberRows` does', 'Iterates exactly the values `edgePlacements` does'), so one encoder is what makes that claim structural. Drop the `placementKey` import (:34) and key the first two by `nestedAddress`, which :41 already imports; the doc references at :500 and :533 name `placementKey` and re-point with it.

The placement/extent coverage the fold must leave byte-identical — `placed_edges` at :1648-:1668 (placed, via-leaf, observed-empty, unobserved-absent, filled-empty) and `rendered_lines`/`rendered_chars` at :874, :1247, :1375, :1693, :1718-:1727. The fold emits no different row, so these are the regression surface, and this is the pin site if build finds a decidable one to add.

summary: `placementKey` re-spells the nested-member address triple that `member-address.ts` is the declared one home for, so emit keys one set of values two ways.

tests.asserts: under the single encoder every composed value's placement and extent still lands on its own `nested_member` row — the existing `placed_edges` and `rendered_lines`/`rendered_chars` assertions unchanged

acceptance: `pnpm --dir sdk test` green (strict `tsc` + `node --test`) with `placementKey` gone from the authored tree (`rg -a placementKey sdk/src sdk/test` empty) and every `placed_edges`/`rendered_lines`/`rendered_chars` assertion unchanged — the fold emits no different row.
notes: Found by the posture sweep at `sdk/src/declarations.ts`. Output-neutral: the key is an in-memory Map key, never serialized, so the only decidable pin is the deletion — after the fold no second speller compiles. `buildTapHookDedupeKey` (:965) is a third encoder of the same technique, but its concept is a hook member's (event, matcher) identity, so it is routed to `(hook-member-identity)` rather than folded here. scoped at bf809e1b
